analyst_view.overall: Osasuna (16th, 12 pts, one win in their last five) host bottom side Málaga (20th, 5 pts, still without a league win) at El Sadar on Sunday evening, a relegation game both need; Arrasate's Osasuna drew 1-1 with Athletic last time out and Málaga lost 1-2 at home to Racing with ten men. Osasuna miss goalkeeper Aitor Fernández (Sergio Herrera starts) and left-back Bretones (soleus, at least two weeks; in the numbers), with Diego Rico likely at left-back after a week and a half of individual work; Oroz, Herrando and Del Castillo are back in the squad but none is sure to start, and Budimir leads the line. Málaga have Aznou suspended and miss Rafita, Ochoa and Lobete (in the numbers), and since the last view centre-back Calero has become a doubt with a hamstring overload (not in the numbers); Diego Murillo, whom the numbers still list as out, is training fully and could replace him, and Puga and Juan Cruz are back. Ricardo De Burgos referees, and the numbers already take cards off for his short, quiet record this season.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.8 goals and already give Málaga a small boost for Bretones being out. Since the last view Málaga's back line got thinner: Aznou is banned and centre-back Calero missed Saturday's training with a hamstring overload, which the numbers don't know, while Oroz is back to feed Budimir; Murillo being fit softens that, so I move from a small trim to a small rise, about 2.9.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.3 corners, with both sides' recent corner counts already counted. Osasuna cross a lot from Rubén García and Raúl Moro for Budimir and Rico should be fit at left-back, while Málaga, without a win, must come forward; nothing new points either way, so I stay at 10.3.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.3 cards; they add Osasuna's recent cards (19 in six), take some off Málaga's quieter run and take 7% off for referee Ricardo De Burgos, who has shown 3.2 cards a game in four matches this season. They make no adjustment for the stakes, and a 16th-versus-20th relegation game with a bottom side forced to take risks tends to be scrappy, so I keep a small lean up, to about 4.5.

shots.text: The numbers say 30.6 shots and already add a lot for both sides' recent shooting and how much each concedes (about +11% each). Oroz's return and a patched-up Málaga defence point a little higher, but Del Castillo is not expected to start and a nervy game can slow things down, so I stay at 30.6.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target, with Málaga's recent accuracy (33 on target in six) and Osasuna's slightly quieter run already counted. Budimir is fit and Málaga may field a reshuffled defence without Aznou and possibly Calero, but I already give that a little through goals, so I stay at 9.6.
